taxonomic_note: Accepted by ITIS and USDA GRIN; current Flora of North America recognizes Tetragonotheca texana as one of four North American species in the genus.
look_here_first: Flip the flower head over. The quickest field mark is the involucre: the four broad outer phyllaries form a conspicuous square/collar-like base around the head. Then confirm the yellow ray florets, large disc florets with paleae, and the leafy upright habit.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Purola Preserve natural-flora list documents Tetragonotheca texana as naturally occurring. Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County Asteraceae herbarium index includes T. texana. Kerr — Kerr Wildlife Management Area vascular flora documents T. texana with voucher collections.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: County evidence comes from natural-flora/herbarium/WMA sources. Joey frames support morphology only and are not used as range proof.

best_field_traits: upright perennial herb with leafy stems
leaves mostly cauline, opposite in much of the genus; local plants can have irregularly toothed to pinnatifid blades
outer four involucral bracts/phyllaries broad and conspicuous, producing the characteristic squarebud/collar appearance
inner phyllaries smaller and more scarious
receptacle paleate, with a sharp bract/palea subtending individual disc florets
morphology_keys.family_training: High-value Asteraceae teaching species: identify the family from the capitulum/ray+disc architecture, then use the underside of the head—the square outer phyllaries/involucre—as the genus/species-level field shortcut.
morphology_keys.video_training: Joey explicitly flips the head over and uses the four broad square-ish phyllaries as the diagnostic cue among several similar yellow composites.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Do not use yellow rays alone. Tetragonotheca texana announces itself from below: four broad outer phyllaries make a boxy/square collar. Tetraneuris instead emphasizes narrow foliage and a conventional multi-series involucre; Thelesperma has threadlike divided leaves.
